ANALYSIS: "Malignant melanoma" and "melanoma" are synonymous in clinical usage. While "melanoma" is the standard, concise term (e.g., WHO classification, AJCC staging, ICD-11), the addition of "malignant" is redundant but not incorrect — historically used to distinguish it from benign melanocytic lesions (e.g., melanocytic nevus). All melanomas are inherently malignant by definition; there is no benign or low-grade variant. Thus, "melanoma" fully and accurately captures the reference diagnosis without loss of meaning or specificity.
